description: Each trader type's size is the number of transaction records belonging to traders of that type.

a.request: Match each transaction record to its trader (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match) and drop records with no matching trader. Then, for each trader type (`tradekind`), count the transaction records. Count every record, so a trader with five records adds five. Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
a.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM transactionrecord r JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM per) SELECT p.tradekind AS trader_type, p.cnt AS record_count, (p.cnt * 1.0) / s.total_cnt AS share_of_total, p.cnt - s.avg_cnt AS diff_from_average FROM per p CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE s.avg_cnt IS NOT NULL AND p.cnt > s.avg_cnt

c.request: Using the transaction records matched to their traders (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match, dropping records with no matching trader), how big is each trader type (`tradekind`) in this data? Traders with no type form their own group. Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing. Each trader type's size is the number of transaction records belonging to traders of that type.
c.sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM transactionrecord tr JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM counts) SELECT c.tradekind, c.cnt AS count, (c.cnt * 1.0) / s.total_cnt AS share_of_total, c.cnt - s.avg_cnt AS diff_from_average FROM counts c CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE s.avg_cnt IS NOT NULL AND c.cnt > s.avg_cnt

b.request: For each trader type (`tradekind`, with null types grouped together), count the transaction records belonging to traders of that type (joined on `trdref` = `tradereg`, unmatched records dropped), then return the types whose count is strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts, showing the type, its count, its count divided by the sum of all per-type counts, and its count minus the average, unrounded, with no rows if the average is null
b.sql: WITH per_type AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM transactionrecord r JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM per_type) SELECT p.tradekind, p.cnt AS transaction_count, CAST(p.cnt AS REAL) / s.total_cnt AS share_of_total, p.cnt - s.avg_cnt AS diff_from_avg FROM per_type p CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE s.avg_cnt IS NOT NULL AND p.cnt > s.avg_cnt

d.request: Using the transaction records matched to their traders (`trdref` = `tradereg`, exact text match, dropping records with no matching trader), how big is each trader type (`tradekind`), where a trader type's size is the number of transaction records belonging to traders of that type, and where traders with no type form their own group? Which trader types have a count strictly above the plain average of the per-type counts? For each one, show the trader type, its count, that count divided by the total of all the per-type counts, and the count minus the average. Don't round anything, and return nothing if the average is missing.
d.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM transactionrecord r JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), stats AS (SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt FROM per) SELECT p.tradekind, p.cnt AS count, p.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt AS share_of_total, p.cnt - s.avg_cnt AS diff_from_avg FROM per p CROSS JOIN stats s WHERE s.avg_cnt IS NOT NULL AND p.cnt > s.avg_cnt
